opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 19% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 51% YoY — the fastest-growing cost line.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 6% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $135.56 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — while other income added $13.08 and the tax benefit added $0.55, leaving a $21.93 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $774,699K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $71.0M (a 9% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $275.5M, other income added $101.3M and the tax benefit added $4.3M, so the chart draws the remaining $169.9M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.
oneTimers: $320.3M of stock-based compensation-related charges (including about $11.0M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions), excluded from non-GAAP results.
$23.4M of amortization of acquired intangibles, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
$2.8M of expenses associated with acquisitions and strategic investments, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $101.3M, net: $53.8M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, plus $47.5M of other income, net — including a $45.7M net realized and unrealized gain on strategic investments in equity securities (per the cash-flow statement). The income tax line was a $4.3M benefit. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $169.4M (EPS -$0.51), after $0.6M of loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 33% YoY and 95% of all revenue; product gross profit was $545.3M, a 74% margin.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 9% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $12.4M gross loss).

sources.label: 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2024 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 33% to $738.1M, the net revenue retention rate was 131%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 41% to $5.2B. Snowflake guided Q1 FY25 product revenue to $745–$750M, up 26–27%, at a 3% non-GAAP operating margin, and full-year FY25 product revenue to $3,250M, up 22%.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $275.5M, wider than the $239.8M loss a year ago. The main reason: $320.3M of stock-based compensation-related charges, including about $11.0M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $71.0M, a 9% margin (up from 6% a year ago).
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 461 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+39% YoY) and 691 Forbes Global 2000 customers (+8% YoY). Operating cash flow was $344.6M and adjusted free cash flow was $324.3M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 32% to $774.7M, with product revenue up 33% to $738.1M — but $320.3M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $275.5M and a net loss of $169.9M.
